subject: one chain is not converging with the others

messages.author: f525118bc47870b3
messages.subject: one chain is not converging with the others
parts:
Dear Stan Experts,

I persistently run in the following problem, when I try to estimate more complex (possibly overparameterized) reinforcement learning models: one of the default 4 chains (2000 samples each, 1000 warmup) is/are consistenly “off” from the others usually malingering at the boudary of the parameter range. For example, when trying to estimate learning rates (range 0-1), one chain is sampling at or near zero, whereas the other 3 are in a normal (i.e. expected) range of around 0.6. The attached density and trace plot clearly exemplify the problem. Moreover, it is always a different chain that is “off” when I look at different parameters.

The question is: what can I do about it? Are there any specific settings to the HMC sampler that I can adjust to avoid 1 chain being stuck, even if that means I have to sample each chain longer?

Back in my JAGS/runjags days, I could examine the chains and then extend the sampling at the point where I left off. I could also drop one of the chains. This was convenient to a certain extent, but it did not help with the problem of different chains being “off” for different parameters. Is something like this even advisable, or am I breaking some of the fundamental rules of MCMC sampling?

I have coded some post-processing functions in R that try to guess if a posterior distribution is bimodal due to one chain being "off" and — based on this judgment — attempts to remove the outlyling chain by replacing the samples of NA. I recoded parts of the WAIC function to deal with NAs in the log_lik parameter. Interestingly, this always results in a slightly higher WAIC (about 5 points) than the original model. Furthermore, I also recompute posterior point estimates (mean,map,median) based on these adjusted chains, which I need for further analyses. I would like to know, if the experts think this is a practical, but also viable solution to deal with the problem or whether this is totally absurd.

Thanks a lot,
Jan

PS: attached are exemplary density and trace plots (these are actually the group posteriors, but I see this also with posteriors for individual subjects) and the stan model file that consistently produces this erratic behavior.

messages.author: f525118bc47870b3
messages.subject: Re: one chain is not converging with the others
parts:
I just realized that the examples in the figures are not the actually learning rates, but rather the common means of the Matt trick, which is used to compute the actual learning rates (see stan file for details).

Thanks for giving this your consideration.
Jan
